name: Comment annotation polish: spacing, View on GitHub, no-wrap menu, expanding reply
description: Polish for the inline PR comment thread: tightened reply-box spacing, added "View on GitHub" to the overflow menu, stopped that menu wrapping, and made the reply prompt expand into the full markdown editor (GitHub-style) with reliable focus.

steps.title: Tighten reply-box spacing
steps.body: Cut the reply box top margin to **4px** and the thread-actions bar to **6px** margin + **6px** padding (verified the exact gaps in an isolated repro).

steps.title: Add "View on GitHub" to the comment menu
steps.body: The overflow (•••) menu now always renders and exposes **View on GitHub**, opening the comment's permalink via `window.api.shell.openExternal`. Delete moves behind a separator when deletable.

steps.title: Stop the menu wrapping its text
steps.body: The shared content sizes to the anchor (the tiny ••• button) floored at 128px, so "View on GitHub" wrapped. Fixed locally with `w-auto!` (important needed because tailwind-merge v2.6 doesn't merge the v4 `w-(...)` syntax). Verified in a faithful absolute-positioned repro: before 128px/2 lines, after ~145px/1 line.

steps.title: Reply prompt expands into the full editor
steps.body:
Mirrors GitHub: the reply affordance starts as a slim one-line prompt; clicking (or focusing) it swaps in the same **MarkdownComposer** (Write/Preview + toolbar) the new-comment composer uses, with **Cancel**/**Reply** actions. Cmd/Ctrl+Enter posts, Esc cancels, collapses + clears after a successful post.

Focus fix: Carta's `autoFocus` only fires on initial page load, so a dynamically-mounted editor (the expanded reply) never grabbed focus. MarkdownComposer now focuses its internal `<textarea>` imperatively on mount when `autofocus` is set — which also firms up the new-comment composer.

callouts.body: Expanded branch reuses MarkdownComposer; collapsed branch is a readonly input that expands on focus/click.
Imperative focus on the next frame (Carta renders the textarea during its own mount), replacing the unreliable autoFocus attribute for dynamically-mounted editors.
